candidates.statement: This guidance describes FDA’s policies regarding compliance with current good manufacturing 18 practice (CGMP) requirements for facilities that compound human drugs and register with FDA 19 as outsourcing facilities under section 503B of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act 20 (FD&C Act). Under section 501(a)(2)(B) of the FD&C Act, a drug is deemed to be adulterated if 21 it is not produced in accordance with CGMP. FDA’s regulations regarding CGMP requirements 22 for the preparation of drug products have been established in 21 CFR parts 210 and 211. 2 FDA 23 intends to promulgate more specific CGMP regulations for outsourcing facilities. Until these 24 final regulations are promulgated, outsourcing facilities are subject to the CGMP requirements in 25 parts 210 and 211. This guidance provides for conditions under which FDA generally does not 26 intend to take regulatory action against an outsourcing facility regarding certain CGMP 27 requirements in parts 210 and 211 during this interim period. This guidance applies to drugs 28 compounded in accordance with section 503B. In addition, this guidance generally applies to 29 drugs that outsourcing facilities repackage and biological products that outsourcing facilities 30 mix, dilute, or repackage in accordance with relevant guidance for outsourcing facilities. 3

candidates.context: This guidance revises the draft guidance Current Good Manufacturing Practice—Interim 38 Guidance for Human Drug Compounding Outsourcing Facilities Under Section 503B of the 39 FD&C Act issued in July 2014. Revision 1 was developed to (1) include considerations for non- 40 sterile compounded drug products; (2) differentiate between requirements applicable to sterile 41 compounded drug products and non-sterile compounded drug products where appropriate; (3) 42 include changes regarding stability testing, including the assignment of a beyond-use date (BUD) 43 as an expiration date, and release testing requirements; and (4) address reserve samples and 44 provide guidance on “in-use times.” Revision 2 refines a description of antimicrobial 45 effectiveness testing in section III.K. and clarifies that section C of appendix B does not apply to 46 non-sterile unpreserved aqueous drug products. 4

candidates.statement: The Drug Quality and Security Act added a new section 503B to the FD&C Act. 4 Under section 58 503B(b), a compounder can register as an outsourcing facility with FDA. Drug products 59 compounded in an outsourcing facility can qualify for exemptions from the FDA approval 60 requirements in section 505 of the FD&C Act, 5 the requirement to label drug products with 61 adequate directions for use under section 502(f)(1) of the FD&C Act, 6 and the drug supply chain 62 security requirements in section 582 of the FD&C Act, 7 if the conditions in section 503B are 63 met. Outsourcing facilities are inspected by FDA according to a risk-based schedule and must 64 comply with other provisions of the FD&C Act, including CGMP requirements under section 65 501(a)(2)(B) (see section 503B). 66
